answer: Give the network a few independent inlets instead of one open door. Each admission gateway vets newcomers with its own checks and stakes its own standing on every identity it lets through; if its admits turn out to be a sybil tide, the gateway loses its licence and its reputation. A pearl among fakes is then traceable to the inlet that passed it, so gateways compete to filter hard and farms cannot shop for the weakest door without the cost surfacing.
